themes_detail.label: Street Signs Vanishing/Damaged
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints—both missing and damaged—spiked dramatically THIS WEEK, with 8 damaged sign complaints filed this week alone vs. a baseline of 1.2 per week, and 7 missing sign complaints last week vs. 1.4 per week baseline, suggesting either deliberate damage, theft, or a citywide maintenance failure affecting UES navigation and traffic safety.
evidence: Street Sign - Damaged: 8 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly baseline (540% spike, z-score 4.85)
Street Sign - Missing: 7 complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly baseline (409% spike, z-score 5.67)
Combined pattern suggests coordinated issue rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Are street signs being systematically removed or vandalized? Interview DOT about UES patrols and sign replacement timelines.
Map the geographic pattern: are signs disappearing from specific corridors (e.g., near parks, commercial strips, transit hubs)?

themes_detail.label: Lead Exposure Spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints jumped to 23 filed last week vs. 8.1 per week baseline (183% spike, z-score 5.14)—a significant public health concern THIS WEEK given the UES's aging housing stock and proximity to schools, requiring urgent investigation into whether this reflects a specific building failure or broader remediation gap.
evidence: Lead complaints: 23 last week vs. 8.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (183% spike, z-score 5.14)
UES contains pre-1960 housing stock vulnerable to lead paint and pipes (per CB budget requests for housing renovations)
Escalation occurred in single week, suggesting possible test results or enforcement action trigger
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Health Department and HPD: was there a spike in lead testing results last week? Any enforcement actions filed?
Profile families in affected buildings; interview pediatricians about childhood lead screening rates on UES.

themes_detail.label: Helicopter Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Helicopter noise complaints skyrocketed 8700% THIS PERIOD—from 0.1 per week baseline to 11 complaints 3 weeks ago (z-score 32.88, highest statistical anomaly in dataset)—indicating either a specific operational change (medical flights, tours, news crews) or temporary event that warrants immediate investigation into FAA coordination and resident impact.
evidence: Noise - Helicopter: 11 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (8700% spike, z-score 32.88, highest severity)
Spike is temporally defined (3 weeks ago), suggesting event-driven rather than chronic
UES includes East Side Heliport on East 34th Street, vulnerable to airspace activity changes
reporting_angles: Contact FAA and heliport operator: were there operational changes, charter increases, or emergency medical flights 3 weeks ago?
Investigate whether news crews or helicopter tours ramped up coverage of a specific UES story (construction, incident, event).

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Enforcement Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints surged to 10 filings last week vs. 2.4 weekly baseline (321% spike, z-score 4.61)—a sharp escalation tied to the district's post-pandemic dining landscape and suggesting either resident pushback against shed encroachment, noise, or sanitation issues, or a new enforcement campaign by the city.
evidence: Outdoor Dining complaints: 10 last week vs. 2.4 weekly baseline (321% spike, z-score 4.61)
Aligns with recent local news coverage of cannabis dispensaries (Maryjane, AVA Flower Co) suggesting UES commercial sector activity
Spike is recent and localized, not a sustained trend
reporting_angles: Interview Community Board 8 about outdoor dining permits: have violations increased or are complaints driven by specific problem venues?
Identify which blocks/restaurants are generating complaints; visit to assess shed conditions, noise, sanitation.

themes_detail.label: Public Urination & Park Rule Violations
themes_detail.summary: Two related quality-of-life spikes emerged over the past 2-3 weeks: urinating in public (3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 baseline, +2300%, z-score 8.69) and park rule violations (5 complaints last week vs. 0.4 baseline, +1233%, z-score 9.55), suggesting either enforcement changes, user pattern shifts in Central Park or neighborhood green spaces, or a transient population concentration.
evidence: Urinating in Public: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Violation of Park Rules: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (1233% spike, z-score 9.55)
Parallel timing suggests either coordinated enforcement or underlying population/usage shift
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department and NYPD: did enforcement in Central Park or neighborhood parks change in the past 2 weeks?
Interview precinct captains: are there new homeless encampments or transient activity on UES blocks? Any outreach programs active?
